description: The prompt selector (PL.core-language-prompt-selector, U110(4) Q4): which object a pick offers for identification (first) or point and name, the one pick prompt standing and the answers it takes, and which object in reach is asked the collection quiz, when (src/language-learning/prompt-selector.ts).
comparison: exact, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent); an unknown op or step is an error, never a skip

cases.name: run: a pick raises one prompt, identification first; the last pick that raised one stands
cases.note: Examine's pick is the nearest object with a role within 5 (x/z): from (0, 9.5) the Fountain, 5.5 away, is out of reach. The well is a target and nameable: it asks identification, not both. The cauldron then stands in its place; a pick that raises nothing (the crate, no word) or picks nothing leaves it standing. Once the well is identified, its pick offers point and name.

cases.name: run: objects that come into reach together are each asked in turn, once per stay; a wrong answer waits for the next stay
cases.note: From (3, 0, 4) all three stalls are within 5 (the bread stall and the anvil exactly 5). One quiz stands until it is chosen, right or wrong; then the next object in reach not yet offered this stay is asked, in registration order. The bread stall, answered wrongly, is not asked again until it has left reach and come back.

cases.name: run: an object that comes into reach while a quiz stands is asked after it; a quiz stands while its object is out of reach
cases.note: The cheese stall and the anvil arrive while the bread stall's quiz stands, and are asked after it. The cheese stall's quiz still stands after the player walks away; answered wrongly there, it is asked again when the stall comes back into reach.

cases.name: run: the game's collection range and options; a knowledge world
run: a quiz carried out of reach and back is the offer of the stay it returns to; answered wrongly there, it is not asked again in that stay
cases.note: PL.core-learning-history-fields (m1-quiz-reasked-same-stay). The bread stall is asked from (-1, 0, 0); the player walks away with its quiz standing and comes back to (2, 0, 2), where all three stalls are in reach: the bread stall counts as offered in this stay (offered [bread_stall]) and the cheese stall and the anvil wait. Answered wrongly, the bread stall is not asked again: the cheese stall is, then the anvil. Only after the bread stall leaves reach and comes back is it asked again.

cases.name: run: a returning standing quiz joins the objects still offered this stay, after them
cases.note: PL.core-learning-history-fields. From (3, 0, 0) all three stalls are in reach. The bread stall is asked and answered wrongly (it stays offered); the cheese stall is asked. At (-1, 0, 0) only the bread stall is in reach: offered keeps it, and the cheese stall's quiz stands out of reach. Back at (3, 0, 0) the cheese stall returns while its quiz stands and is added after the objects still offered (offered [bread_stall, cheese_stall]). Answered wrongly, neither is asked again this stay: the anvil is.
